items.title: ICare-FASTER: point-of-care hs-troponin I cuts ED stay by 47 minutes in suspected MI with no rise in 30-day MI or cardiac death (Circulation)
items.summary: In a six-hospital New Zealand stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial of nearly 60,000 ED presentations, swapping central-lab hs-troponin for a whole-blood point-of-care hs-cTnI assay in the same accelerated rule-out pathway shortened ED length of stay by 13% (47 minutes) with identical 30-day safety (Than et al., Circulation, Oct 19, 2026).
bullets: **ICare-FASTER** (Circulation, 19 Oct 2026): pragmatic **stepped-wedge cluster-randomised** trial of **point-of-care hs-troponin I** in the ED.
**6 sites**, **59,980 presentations** (44,747 people; mean age 61; 49.5% female), Feb 2023-Jan 2025; **31,392** during the intervention.
Both arms used an **accelerated pathway with a single-sample rule-out**; control used a **central-lab hs-cTn**, intervention a **whole-blood point-of-care hs-cTnI**.
**ED length of stay fell 13%** (95% CI 9-16%; p<0.001): **47 minutes** (33-61) from a **376-minute** control mean.
**Safety**: 30-day **MI or cardiac death 0.39% in both arms** (p=0.54).
Message: a faster pathway with the same **30-day MI or cardiac death rate (0.39%)** in a real-world, six-hospital setting.
Caveat: measures ED flow and **30-day** safety at six sites, not long-term outcomes.
